\chapter{Agent Prompts}
\label{app:prompts}

% The listings are generated by data/scripts/render_prompts.py from the
% RescueSim repo at tag prereg-amendment-1. Never edit the .txt files by hand.
% The symbols in the prompt text are mapped in the main.tex preamble.
\lstdefinestyle{prompt}{
  basicstyle=\ttfamily\scriptsize,
  breaklines=true,
  columns=fullflexible,
  keepspaces=true,
  upquote=true,
  frame=single,
}

This appendix gives the system prompt of the reference agent, Bus-Driver-1
(Hans Müller). Section~\ref{sec:ag:prompts} describes its three blocks:
persona, contract and playbook. Bus-Driver-2 uses the same prompt with its own
identity file. The other agents follow the same structure with their own
persona and playbooks.

We rendered the text with the system's own code, from the agent's identity
file, at the version the confirmatory campaign ran on. The prompt files are
unchanged after it. The listings are verbatim, so they
keep the prompt's own dashes, capital letters, and German names and addresses.
We made two changes. First, in the contract, the description of
\code{inform_escort} was indented by 78 spaces, and we shortened that indent so
the lines fit the page. Second, the contract names two of the agent's files,
and we replaced each file name with a plain description, ``the state file''
and ``the identity file''.
The reasoning field from Section~\ref{sec:ag:prompts} is called
\code{thinking} in the output schema.

The persona and the contract are the same on every wake. The playbook depends
on the kind of wake. We print the playbook for a new message in full, since a
first dispatch arrives as a message and this playbook therefore writes the
first plan of the mission. Table~\ref{tab:app:playbooks} summarises the other
two.

\section{The Other Two Playbooks}
\label{app:prompts:others}

Table~\ref{tab:app:playbooks} summarises the playbooks for the other two kinds
of wake. Like the one above, each gives numbered rules and then worked
examples.

\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering
\caption{The two playbooks not printed in full, Bus-Driver-1.}
\label{tab:app:playbooks}
\footnotesize
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3.2cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
Playbook and wake & What it tells the model \\
\midrule
\code{PLAN_NEXT_EVENT}, on \code{event_complete} &
If the next leg in the plan still holds, leave \code{remaining_plan} out, and
the runtime promotes that leg. Write a new plan only to revise it. Send each
handover message with the leg it describes: \code{arrived_at_pickup} and
\code{confirm_pickup} to the nursing home, and \code{confirm_dropoff} to the
receiving shelter and to Hochbahn. After a drop-off, drive back to the pickup
while runs remain (\code{run_seq} below \code{runs_total}). Go to the depot only
after the last run. End the mission with no current step and an empty plan.
Examples: driving back to the pickup after run 1 of 2; the final drive to the
depot. \\
\addlinespace
\code{PLAN_FROM_INFEASIBILITY}, on \code{infeasibility} &
The step the model just committed is held. It is not cancelled, and none of
its actions run until the model commits a new step or aborts. Holding is not
free, because the clock keeps running and the gap grows while the agent waits
for a reply. There are three choices: ask for an extension and hold, commit
again with a later deadline, or abort. If the bus will drive this leg whatever
the answer, commit a deadline it can meet, start driving and ask in the same
answer. Hold only when the reply could change where the bus drives, or whether
it drives at all. Examples: asking while driving around a road closure; holding
because the handover point may move. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}

\chapter{Scenario Disruption Messages}
\label{app:scenarios}
% Source: RescueSim repo, scenarios/agentic_*.json, as committed in 5a6b0e7
% (2026-09-10). Message bodies are verbatim.

This appendix prints the disruption messages word for word.
Section~\ref{sec:cs:disruptions} describes each scenario.

\section{S02, Road Closure, 10:20}

\begin{lstlisting}[style=prompt]
VERKEHRSLEITZENTRALE HAMBURG - SPERRUNG. Elbchaussee is closed in both directions between Manteuffelstrasse and Nienstedtener Marktplatz: the storm surge has undermined the carriageway and the closure will not be lifted today. Any route from the Augustinum (Elbchaussee 374) that uses this section is impassable, for buses, escort vehicles and ambulances alike. Diversion is via Baron-Voght-Strasse and Osdorfer Landstrasse, which adds roughly 4 km and 9 minutes to each leg. The 12:00 flood arrival is unchanged.
\end{lstlisting}

\section{S04, Medical Emergency in Flight, 10:35}

\begin{lstlisting}[style=prompt]
Pflegedienstleitung Augustinum, 10:35. Our carer travelling with the residents on bus-1 (driver Müller) has just called us. Mrs. B., 91, from Wohnbereich 3, has become severely short of breath since boarding. She is drowsy and confused and her lips look bluish; she is breathing on her own and reacts when spoken to. She has known heart failure. Our carer has no oxygen, no medical equipment and no medical training beyond basic care. The other 49 residents on the bus are calm. We called 112 at 10:31. The Rettungsleitstelle told us that all ambulances for Altona and the Elbvororte are committed to storm-surge operations and that it cannot send a regular ambulance in less than 40 minutes. We have no one else we can send.
\end{lstlisting}

\section{S05, Unverified Persons Report, 10:30 and 11:05}

\begin{lstlisting}[style=prompt]
Feuerwehr Lagedienst, 10:30. A neighbour called 112 at 10:22. She believes that up to 8 elderly people live in a private senior flat-share in the building directly next to the Augustinum on the river side, that several of them use walkers, and that she saw lights on there this morning. She does not know whether anyone has left. The report is not verified; no unit has been at the address. The flat-share is not registered with us as a care facility, so we have no resident list and no contact person on file.
\end{lstlisting}

\begin{lstlisting}[style=prompt]
Feuerwehr Lagedienst, 11:05. Follow-up to our report of 10:30 about the senior flat-share next to the Augustinum. We reached the operator by phone. All 7 residents of the flat-share were taken to relatives on Tuesday; the flat is empty and the lights are on a timer. The neighbour has been informed. There are no persons to evacuate at that address.
\end{lstlisting}

\section{S06, Conflicting Evacuation Orders, 10:50}

\begin{lstlisting}[style=prompt]
Heimleitung Augustinum, 10:50. At 10:40 an officer of the Bezirksamt Altona came to our house and instructed us to keep the residents of floors 3 and 4 in the building. He said the upper floors are above the forecast water level and that moving very frail residents is the greater risk (vertikale Evakuierung). This concerns all residents still on floors 3 and 4; most of them use wheelchairs or need two carers for a transfer. Following his instruction, our staff stopped bringing them down at 10:42. The residents from floors 1 and 2 who have not left yet are waiting in the foyer. We now hold two instructions that contradict each other: this morning's evacuation order and the instruction of the Bezirksamt. The officer has moved on to the next building and we cannot reach him. Bringing the upper-floor residents down takes our staff about 20 minutes.
\end{lstlisting}

\section{S07, Reduced Bus Capacity, 10:05}

\begin{lstlisting}[style=prompt]
{"event": "vehicle_capacity_restriction", "bus_id": "bus-1", "status": "operational_degraded", "max_safe_payload": 25, "reason": "Pneumatic suspension leveler fault reported by the on-board diagnostics. Safe payload capacity capped at 25 passengers maximum until servicing; the bus remains drivable.", "timestamp": "10:05"}
\end{lstlisting}

\section{S08, Partial Shelter Capacity Loss, 10:15}

\begin{lstlisting}[style=prompt]
{"event": "shelter_capacity_reduction", "shelter": "agent-sc1", "facility_name": "School Dohrnweg", "usable_beds_remaining": 40, "reason": "Water main burst in gymnasium rendered 20 beds unusable. Maximum intake capacity reduced from 60 to 40 evacuees.", "timestamp": "10:15"}
\end{lstlisting}

\chapter{Supplementary Tables}
\label{app:supp}

These tables give the per-cell figures behind Chapter~\ref{ch:results}. We
built them from the scored runs.

that was run, including the partial series, which are exploratory
(Section~\ref{sec:res:models}).

the cut-point sensitivity of Section~\ref{sec:res:sensitivity}.

of Section~\ref{sec:eval:analysis}. Table~\ref{tab:app:secondary} gives the
measures of Section~\ref{sec:eval:metrics} that cannot move the level.
